clue.text: Got more polished?

definitions.meaning: to wax is to grow larger, as the moon does, so this means increased
a floor or car rubbed with polish to make it shine has been treated this way

explanation.surface: A question about whether something has been given a better shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxing is growing, as the moon grows, and also applying a shining polish, so one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Tax return, perhaps, that is eagerly awaited

definitions.text: Tax return, perhaps, that is eagerly awaited

parts.words: Tax return, perhaps, that is eagerly awaited
parts.note: not the form filed with the taxman but the money he hands back, which every taxpayer longs to receive

explanation.surface: A taxpayer waiting anxiously for the outcome of their annual form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax return' looks like the paperwork; read it as tax being returned, money paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Overpaid tax handed back is a repayment, the kind of return a taxpayer hopes for.

clue.text: The property Cinderella's stepsisters shared

parts.note: property here is not land or a house but a quality; in the fairy tale both stepsisters are famously unattractive

explanation.surface: A legal question about an inheritance divided between two sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' suggests real estate; it means a characteristic, the plainness the pantomime 'Ugly Sisters' share.
explanation.definitionFit: The stepsisters are known as the Ugly Sisters, so their shared quality is lack of beauty.

clue.text: Separate parts of a defunct body

definitions.text: Separate parts of a defunct body

parts.words: Separate parts of a defunct body
parts.note: a defunct body sounds like a dissolved organisation, but it is a corpse whose parts an anatomist cuts apart

explanation.surface: Breaking up the remaining assets of an organisation that has folded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defunct body' reads as a wound-up society; it is a dead body on an anatomist's table.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist cuts a cadaver into pieces to study it, which is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Rose to a higher position as the century came to a close

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so a century
came to a close means finished, or ended

explanation.surface: Someone climbed the social ladder just as the hundred years ran out.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or go up to a higher place is a synonym of rising.

clue.text: It might well be a terrific bore!

definitions.text: It might well be a terrific bore!

parts.words: It might well be a terrific bore!
parts.note: a bore is not a dull person but a surge of water running up a river, and terrific means terrifying here

explanation.surface: Complaining about a tedious person who will not stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is a large wave forcing its way up an estuary, like the Severn Bore in England; 'terrific' carries its old sense of frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge, frightening surge of sea water is a natural cousin of the river bore.

clue.text: Theoretically a profit appearing in a different form

indicators.note: the word appearing is to be put into another shape, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant notes a profit that only shows up when figures are presented another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different form' rearranges APPEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain on paper is a rise in value not yet realised by selling, so it exists only in theory.

clue.text: A prison showing signs of unrest?

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail where the inmates are getting restless.
explanation.walkthrough: STIR is old slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and about, in motion or excitement, is the adverb's sense of agitation.

clue.text: Trees dotted along an indented coast

definitions.meaning: laurels, the trees whose leaves crowned victors
inlets of the sea scattered along a jagged shoreline

explanation.surface: Trees scattered along a ragged stretch of shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurel trees share their name with the wide curving inlets that notch a coastline.

clue.text: MPs empowered to act for others

definitions.text: MPs empowered to act for others

parts.words: MPs empowered to act for others
parts.note: members of parliament elected to represent constituents, and also people authorised to stand in for someone

explanation.surface: Members of parliament given authority to represent their voters.
explanation.walkthrough: In France, MPs are called by this word; generally it means stand-ins with delegated power.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a lower house in many countries carry this title, as do assistants authorised to act on another's behalf.

clue.text: Simian chap who's a specialist in physical education?

definitions.meaning: a primitive man resembling an ape

definitions.text: who's a specialist in physical education?
definitions.meaning: read as '...', PE being physical education, someone who teaches gym

explanation.surface: Describing a gym teacher as rather apelike.
explanation.definitionFit: A primitive ape-like human ancestor, or split differently, a gym teacher.

clue.text: Move gradually away from the centre

definitions.meaning: to inch or creep forward little by little
the rim or border, as far from the middle as possible

explanation.surface: Instructions to shuffle slowly towards the outside of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep along by small steps, and also the rim or margin far from the middle.

clue.text: Add up converse in a mood of dejection?

indicators.note: the opposite of the direction word is wanted, so the second part is swapped for its contrary

parts.note: to cast up a column of figures is to total it

explanation.surface: A gloomy person told to do some arithmetic and to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'cast up' is an old phrase for adding up; 'converse' (opposite) turns UP into DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cast down is an idiom for feeling depressed and downhearted.

clue.text: Thinks a lot of events are badly organised

indicators.note: events that are poorly arranged have their order jumbled

explanation.surface: Complaining that functions are poorly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly organised' shuffles EVENTS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere or hold in deep respect is to have a high opinion of someone.

clue.text: A set-back about metrical composition

parts.note: re means about or concerning
poetry written in metre is verse

explanation.surface: A setback in writing a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeat or misfortune is a synonym for a setback, as in suffering a military loss.

clue.text: Persuasive in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Persuasive in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Persuasive in a manner of speaking
parts.note: the stock phrase 'in a manner of speaking' means 'so to say', but here it literally describes a persuasive way of talking

explanation.surface: A hedge: something is sort of persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge; take it literally, persuasive in how one speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, forceful speech that wins people over is the mark of a gifted orator.

clue.text: Daring aerobatic swoop on a shady resort?

definitions.meaning: a plunge by a stunt plane down close to the ground
a disreputable bar or club, a seedy haunt

explanation.surface: A stunt pilot swoops down over a dubious holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt plane's plunge near the ground, and slang for a seedy drinking den.

clue.text: Exaggerated result of placing a unit outside the ruins of Dover

indicators.note: the unit is placed beyond, after, the rearranged letters
the name Dover is wrecked, its letters rearranged

parts.note: one is a single unit

explanation.surface: Someone placing a figure outside the ruins of the Kent port, overstating things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' rearranges DOVER to OVERD; 'outside' puts ONE after it. Dover is a port town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid on too thick, taken to excess, is overplayed.

clue.text: Wreck that's reassembled with little hesitation

indicators.note: the letters of that's are put together again in a new order

parts.note: er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A wrecked object put back together while someone stammers a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassembled' rearranges THATS to SHATT; ER is a hesitant 'um'.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash or destroy completely is to break into pieces.

clue.text: His model, much damaged, lay in ruins

indicators.note: the words his model are badly broken, so their letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man's model was smashed and left wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much damaged' rearranges HIS MODEL. 'Lay' looks like a past tense; it is the verb 'to lay in ruins'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze or knock down a building completely is to reduce it to rubble.

clue.text: The day that revealed Brutus ugly side?

indicators.note: ugly signals that the word side is twisted into another shape

explanation.surface: A day that showed the nasty side of Brutus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' rearranges SIDE. Brutus showed his treachery when Caesar was stabbed on the 15th of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of March in the Roman calendar was when Brutus joined in killing Caesar.

clue.text: Fact-demanding educational paper?

parts.note: not a journal for teachers but a test paper that requires students to recall facts

explanation.surface: A scholarly journal that insists on facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Educational paper' suggests a journal; it is a test sat in school.
explanation.definitionFit: A written test set to students demands they reproduce facts.

clue.text: Lets everybody sow discord

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: discord means disorder, so the letters of sow are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Everyone is permitted to stir up strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' rearranges SOW into OWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Permits, a verb meaning to grant permission, is a synonym of lets.

clue.text: Amusingly odd master turning left

indicators.note: turning means the word for master is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a master

explanation.surface: A whimsical master who takes a left turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses LORD to DROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky, dry humour that is whimsical and funny is described with this word.

clue.text: An outwardly sharp-witted ruler who failed to get command of the sea

definitions.text: ruler who failed to get command of the sea

indicators.note: the word for sharp-witted sits outwardly, around the 'An'

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever king who could not order the tide back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts CUTE round AN. The English king Cnut, in legend, ordered the tide back to show courtiers it would not obey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish-English king of legend commanded the tide to halt and it rolled in regardless.

clue.text: They're not much catch if you want a bite

definitions.text: They're not much catch if you want a bite

parts.words: They're not much catch if you want a bite
parts.note: the fish an angler lands are so small they would make a poor meal; bite is both a fish taking bait and a snack

explanation.surface: Unsuitable romantic partners for anyone hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not much catch' suggests a poor match; read it as tiny fish, little use for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fish such as minnows are a poor haul for an angler hoping to eat.

clue.text: Nerve-racked science-fiction writer

indicators.note: racked means tortured or wrenched, so the letters of nerve are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: An anxious science-fiction author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racked' rearranges NERVE. Jules Verne wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules is the French novelist of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, a pioneer of the genre.

clue.text: Stingy toff filled with good intentions?

parts.note: mean means stingy
a swell is a fashionable upper-class gentleman, a toff

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted aristocrat brimming with kind purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'toff' is British slang for a posh upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose intentions are kind even if the results disappoint.
